text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

RTZ-CRA Ltd yesterday announced the sale of its A$1.1 billion Century zinc project to Pasminco Ltd for A$345 million, one day after the Queensland Government put a freeze on development of all pastoral leases and stopped issuing and renewing most new mining leases as a result of the High Court's Wik native title decision. Page 1.

The metal industry can claim another pace-setting wage settlement after BTR Nylex subsidiary Hawker de Havilland agreed to pay rises of 17 to 18 per cent over two years for its workers at the airframe component maker's Sydney plant. The deal follows ACI packaging's promise of pay rises of 16 per cent by mid-1997 and BHP Steel's offer to 20,000 employees of pay rises totalling 15 per cent over two years. Page 1.

County NatWest has launched the first funds in the Australian retail funds management industry to abolish all entry and exit fees. The funds also have significantly lower annual fees at 1.3 per cent and will be mostly delivered over the Internet, in a move to avoid overhead costs. Page 1.

Aluminium producer Alcoa of Australia Ltd has reported a 24 per cent increase in after-tax profit to A$388.3 million for the year to December 31, after boosting sales to A$2,531 million, up 6.4 per cent from A$2,379 million. Alcoa finance director Phillip Spry-Bailey said the result was solid given the volatility of the year, the ups and downs of the LME and metal prices. Page 21.

In a move that will expand facilities to develop 116 billion cubic feet of gas and 10 million barrels of condensate net to the company, BHP Petroleum Ltd has won board approval to spend A$132 million for the second phase of development of the Bruce oil and gas field in the North Sea. Page 21.

The market price of gold dropped a further US$3 to US$354 an ounce yesterday in New York as United States hedge funds continued their pressure on the bullion by taking new short positions in late European trading. The fall hit Plutonic Resources shares, which lost 1c to A$5.15 and Gawler Craton star Helix fell 5c to A$3.25. Page 21.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Mining giant RTZ-CRA has sold its stake in the proposed A$1.1 billion Century Zinc mine in north-west Queensland for A$345 million following months of delays over native title disputes. However, the sale to Melbourne-based Pasminco is conditional as it wil not be finalised until the mine clears land claim hurdles and gains a mining lease. Page 23.

The A$2.65 billion Advance Bank Ltd -St George Bank Ltd proposed merger cleared its final hurdle when the New South Wales Supreme Court approved the controversial deemed proxy conditions of the scheme of arrangement needed to facilitate the deal. Advance wll now proceed with its two shareholder meetings next week which will consider the final merger steps. Page 23.

Alumina and aluminium producer Alcoa of Australia Ltd predicts a "solid performance" this year after announcing a 15 per cent increase in net profits to A$395 million for the 12 months to December 31. Alcoa achieved a turnover of A$2.5 billion for the period which was the result of higher shipments of export alumina. Page 25.

Seven Network Ltd chairman Kerry Stokes is sitting on a paper profit of over A$60 million on his 18-month-old A$200 million investment in the network after Seven shares rose to their highest level since listing on the stock exchange four years ago. Seven closed yesterday at A$4.39 which indicates that investor confidence in the network has returned after a period of major upheaval. Page 25.

Woolworths Ltd has added its name to a small list of major retailers to defy the downward sales trend over the Christmas period. Woolworths will report the higher sales figures next week for the 28 weeks ending January 5. Meanwhile, David Jones Ltd, Country Road Ltd and Just Jeans Ltd have down-graded half-year profit forecasts because of sluggish Christmas sales. Page 25.

Investment house County NatWest has scored a first with the launch of an Internet web site allowing direct investment into one of three managed funds. County's Investment Management chief executive Nick Birrell said the group had taken advantage of the Australian Securities Commission's vision of embracing the Internet. Page 24.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Melbourne-based Pasminco is set to become a major player in the world's zinc industry following the purchase of RTZ-CRA's stake in the north Queensland Century Zinc project for A$345 million. The deal follows RTZ-CRA being forced to delay development of the A$1.1 billion project last year due to controversy surrounding the project failing to reach a compensation agreement with traditional Aboriginal owners. Page 12.

The Federal Government is downplaying possible tariff cuts to a level of five per cent by 2004 on imported cars after threats from US Ford Motor Company to reduce its investment interests in Australia. The Government moved swiftly to distance itself from the Productivity Commission's recommendations to cut tariffs as local car manufacturers called to ensure cuts don't fall to below 15 per cent. Page 12.

Telstra group managing director Paul Rizzo told a large gathering of stockbrokers yesterday that significant steps had been taken in the past 12 months in preparation for the communication giant's one-third sale through a sharemarket listing. Rizzo said that Telstra's efforts to cut costs across the board by 30 per cent were on track. Page 12.

BHP Petroleum will spend A$132 million for a stake in the expansion of the Bruce oil and gasfield in the UK sector of the North Sea. The capital program will expand the existing Bruce facilities to allow the development of 116 billion cubic-feet of gas and over 62 million barrels of condensate. Page 12.

Amid fears that Newcrest Mining was too exposed to spot prices after closing out two million ounces of forward sales last year and the plunging gold price, the miner yesterday revealed an innovative hedging program covering more than 3.7 million ounces of gold amounting to 44 per cent of its reserves. Page 12.

The Supreme Court yesterday approved the legality and fairness of St George Bank's A$2.6 billion offer for Advance Bank, claiming that only "in the particular circumstances" of the Advance deal was the deemed proxy clause fair. St George is now less than a week away from a successful takeover, with National Australia Bank removing pressure from the deal with its refusal to vote its three per cent stake in Advance. Page 13.
THE AGE

After a shareholders' meeting on Monday to approve changes to Advance Bank's articles of association, St George Bank's A$2.65 billion takeover of Advance will pass its last hurdle following the Supreme Court's approval of the scheme. National Australia Bank appears to have helped the success of the deal by not voting its 3.03 per cent stake against the scheme. Page C1.

After three years of negotiations with Aboriginals over the Century Zinc project in Queensland's remote Gulf of Carpentaria region, RTZ-CRA has decided to sell the A$1.13 billion project, along with the Dugald River zinc deposit to the south-east, to Melburne-based zinc group Pasminco for A$345 million. Page C1.

In contrast with the poor pre-Christmas trading results from Australia's largest fashion retailers, the Daiichi Corp-controlled Brashs home entertainment retailer recorded a strong rise in sales in most product categories, with Victoria, New South Wales and Western Australia posting the strongest growth. Page C1.

With the end of the media accreditation system and the arrival of more competition in the telecommunications industry, Telstra is set to review its estimated A$100 million advertising account and has given several new agencies, including Clemenger Melbourne, J. Walter Thompson, Grey Advertising and Y&R Mattingly, the opportunity to pitch. Page C1.

Despite lower metal prices and a strong dollar in 1996, Alcoa of Australia posted a 15 per cent increase in profit to A$395 million, up from A$343.5 million in 1995. Alcoa's results out do its listed competitor, Comalco, which said last month that based on its performance to the end of November, it was looking at a loss for the December half. Page C1.

Investors showed keen interest in Alliance Gold Mines NL yesterday, following a 50,000-ounce increase in the gold resource base at its Maldon project in central Victoria to 120,000 ounces. The boost comes from exploration of the southern extensions of the Eaglehawk reef. Page C2.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
